body:
I replaced the Parallel call in cross_val_score with a for loop and I still get the crash.

I run the code with n_jobs =10 passed to GridSearch, I have 12 CPU cores.

As I said above: even without `cross_val_score`, I get the same error.
With `n_jobs=2` (the number of real cores) I could not reproduce (yet), though.
I remember seeing something similar over the the summer--my grid searches were randomly crashing.  I _think_ I remember the issue happening when n_jobs was large.
I am hitting this issue too. Is there any workaround for this issue ?. I am using 0.14 version

I could just reproduce it myself on a box with 2 physical cores (4 logical cores with HT):

```
>>> for i in xrange(1000):
...      GridSearchCV(LinearSVC(), param_grid=dict(C=[1, 10]), n_jobs=10, cv=10).fit(iris.data, iris.target)
[Parallel] Pool seems closed
[Parallel] Pool seems closed
[Parallel] Pool seems closed
[Parallel] Pool seems closed
[Parallel] Pool seems closed
[Parallel] Pool seems closed
[Parallel] Pool seems closed
[Parallel] Pool seems closed
[Parallel] Pool seems closed
Traceback (most recent call last):
  File "<ipython-input-17-777eb7a7c476>", line 1, in <module>
    for i in xrange(1000): GridSearchCV(LinearSVC(), param_grid=dict(C=[1, 10]), n_jobs=10, cv=10).fit(iris.data, iris.target)
  File "/Users/ogrisel/code/scikit-learn/sklearn/grid_search.py", line 669, in fit
    return self._fit(X, y, ParameterGrid(self.param_grid))
  File "/Users/ogrisel/code/scikit-learn/sklearn/grid_search.py", line 454, in _fit
    for parameters in parameter_iterable
  File "/Users/ogrisel/code/scikit-learn/sklearn/externals/joblib/parallel.py", line 516, in __call__
    for function, args, kwargs in iterable:
ValueError: generator already executing
```

Note, I could not reproduce it with `SGDClassifier` (maybe it's too fast or too slow on this data to be able to trigger the bug).
The above was obtained on today's sklearn master branch.
I assigned this bug too myself and plan to work on it early next month unless someone beats me to it.
If I pass `n_jobs=-1` I cannot reproduce it either.

Just wanted to chime in add that we've also been getting this error sporadically with sklearn 0.14.1 when using our [skll](https://github.com/EducationalTestingService/skll) command-line utility. It usually seems to happen when using ridge regression for us.
@dan-blanchard do you reproduce it with `n_jobs=-1` or just when you put a `n_jobs` to a value much higher value that the number of CPUs on your host (which is probably a bad thing to do anyway)?

As you can see [here](https://github.com/EducationalTestingService/skll/blob/develop/skll/learner.py#L755-762), we specify `n_jobs`, but we don't let it exceed the number of cores on the machine. In most cases we have `n_jobs` set to 5, and are running on machines with 24 cores.

I just thought of some additional details that might be important for our case. While any individual process that uses `GridSearchCV` will only have `n_jobs` set to 5, we frequently have multiple instances running on the same machine all running their own grid searches at the same time. Since we use Grid Engine for scheduling jobs, we never use more slots than there are CPUs on the machine, but it is possible that the machine is maxed out when this is running.

I'm seeing this error a lot more since we switched to using a custom sub-class of `LeaveOneLabelOut` that filters some IDs out of the folds. Could that somehow be related?

The class is very simple: https://github.com/EducationalTestingService/skll/blob/develop/skll/learner.py#L99-L126

issue.body:
I believe this is strongly related to scikit-learn/scikit-learn#1565, but I can't establish much of a pattern for why it only happens sometimes. I've gotten it in local mode and gridmap mode, for regression and for classification, but not with every dataset.

I will say that the dataset I'm seeing it with the most reliably is one that uses our new `FilteredLeaveOneLabelOut` fold generator, and the unit tests seem to pass, so I'm confused.

body:
So, it turns that this is only an issue with Python 2.x. If you run:

``` python
for i in xrange(1000):
    GridSearchCV(LinearSVC(), param_grid=dict(C=[1, 10]), n_jobs=10, cv=10).fit(iris.data, iris.target)
```

in Python 2 (on a machine with fewer than 10 cores), it crashes as you've reported, but if you use Python 3 it runs without a hitch.

I've also been able to work around the issue we've been having with SKLL by just using Python 3 instead.

I made a gist with a little test script: https://gist.github.com/dan-blanchard/6770178.

I can confirm it happens on 2.7.2 and 2.7.4, but not on 3.3.0.

Thanks @dan-blanchard! I will try to have a look soon if nobody finds a fix earlier. It would help if you could find a reproduction case that only uses [joblib.parallel](http://pythonhosted.org/joblib/parallel.html) and report the bug on the joblib project issues' page directly.

Hi, I just wanted to chime in that I still occasionally encounter this issue, even with Python 3.3. I haven't been able to come up with a reproduction case that causes it every time though. It seems to happen even with the same data somewhat randomly.

Good news @GaelVaroquaux and I fixed a very similarly looking issue here: joblib/joblib#105 . The fix is now in the master of joblib but not yet merged in sklearn.

I can no longer trigger the failure reported by @amueller nor with the gist by @dan-blanchard on my workstation but I am pretty confident that this is the same as the one reported by @bthirion in joblib/joblib#105 as the error messages are the same.

I will try to also fix joblib/joblib#75 today and maybe do a 0.8.0a3 release for joblib to be synced back into scikit-learn either today or later this week.
